semanticComparisons.reasoning: 026 chooses request-time context and retained record lineage instead of static knowledge. The other stems distinguish a generation interface from an embeddings model and a prepared body from transport arguments. Those are different decisions, not renamed policy scenarios. No new verdict is issued for the comparison-only items.

029 combines an explicit null property, a named root and a two-row object array. direct-026 traces dotted aliases in a default one-row array. direct-038 applies aggregate ordering and NULL ON NULL to positional scalar array slots. Shared JSON vocabulary and null terminology do not make these the same fact.

FOR JSON PATH uses dots in output aliases for nesting. OPENJSON default WITH column-name matching treats a dotted name as a literal key unless an explicit path is supplied. The snippets exercise different APIs and opposite dot conventions, not a choice-order or renamed-value duplicate.

The neighboring items respectively test one-layer answer paths, the long-scalar JSON_VALUE limit, case-sensitive property matching and one-layer typed fragment projection. 032 adds an actual JSON-in-string decoding boundary and paired scalar/array output. That is substantive composition, but it remains held because default-schema projection is not excluded.
